title: Avertales - for serious AI role-players with large context
author: harveydarvey76
selftext:
Hi all,

I've just finished an Early Access build of AverTales, an AI storytelling / roleplay platform I've been building for a while. Posting here because the interesting part isn't "chat with an LLM", it's everything I had to build around the LLM to stop long campaigns from falling apart.

**The problem I was trying to solve: you spend a few hundred turns in an AI story, get attached to the world and characters, and then watch them slowly stop being themselves as context fades. Every long-form AI story I tried ended that way, so I built the thing I wanted to play.**



What's actually going on under the hood:



\- Four specialist AI roles per turn instead of one giant prompt. A Narrator writes the scene, a Director tracks goals and hidden threads, a Time Analysis pass advances the in-world clock, and a Memory pass consolidates older turns. The narrator streams immediately; the other passes run as background jobs.

\- Memory that behaves like recall. Every 20 turns, older scenes are compressed into memory cards (pgvector embeddings). Retrieval is hybrid: semantic + keyword + importance + location + recency + reinforcement. Nothing is truncated or pruned; retrieval is capped by card count and ranked by relevance.

\- Knowledge boundaries. Characters don't know about events they never witnessed or heard about.

\- Structured world state, not transcript. Editable lore cards, objectives, relationship history, character reflection (traits, motivations, contradictions derived from evidence), story time in days/hours/minutes, and a "memory matrix" that lets you follow one character's storyline across the whole campaign.

\- Story systems you author: skills with dice-informed checks, tracked values (trust, supplies, a curse, whatever), and triggers with odds and conditions the narrator only fires when the scene fits.

\- You own the canon: reroll, edit either side, prune turns, out-of-character steering.

\- Scenario Studio: describe a premise, answer a few questions, get a playable world with characters, lore, skills, triggers and an opening in minutes.

\- Optional illustrated turns with character references so the same face shows up scene after scene.

It's free to try: every account gets a daily credit allowance, and you can play in plain text without touching image generation. Mature content is supported behind an account-level toggle for adults.

I'd really value feedback from this crowd, especially on the memory/retrieval design and on whether the multi-role architecture is worth its cost versus a single well-crafted prompt. Happy to go into implementation details in the comments.
